page.mentor_intro: Delirium is an acute, fluctuating disturbance of attention and awareness that is usually multifactorial and often preventable. Current guidance centres on team-based multicomponent prevention, and the ICU guideline update could not make a recommendation on antipsychotics to treat it.

teaching_points.claim: Prevention works best as a multicomponent, team-based package across the pre-, intra- and postoperative periods; the ESAIC 2024 update reports such packages reduce the incidence and duration of postoperative delirium.

Surgery-induced inflammation is pathogenic in postoperative delirium. Depth of anaesthesia, adequate analgesia and haemodynamic stability are modifiable by the anaesthetist, whereas length and site of surgery are not.
In ICU adults the 2025 SCCM focused update gave conditional recommendations for dexmedetomidine over propofol for sedation, enhanced mobilisation and rehabilitation over usual care, and melatonin.
The same SCCM update could not issue a recommendation on antipsychotics to treat delirium or on benzodiazepines to treat anxiety.

A 2025 meta-analysis found ramelteon, suvorexant and lemborexant associated with 40-46% relative reductions in delirium prevalence, but certainty was low and mortality and length of stay did not change.
The 2026 APA practice guideline contains 15 statements covering prevention, detection and treatment of delirium in adults.

uncertainties: Whether antipsychotics have any role in treating established delirium (no ICU guideline recommendation).
Comparative efficacy of individual sleep-wake agents: no credible subgroup differences, low-certainty evidence.
mcq_angles: First-line approach to delirium prevention: multicomponent non-drug package versus a single prescribed drug.
ICU sedative choice and delirium: dexmedetomidine versus propofol or benzodiazepines.
What the SCCM update did and did not recommend (melatonin yes, antipsychotic treatment no recommendation).
Modifiable intra-operative contributors to postoperative delirium.

page.mentor_intro: Delirium is acute and fluctuating while dementia is chronic and progressive, but the two coexist often: delirium superimposed on dementia is common in hospitalised older adults and carries worse outcomes than either alone.

teaching_points.claim: Delirium superimposed on dementia (DSD) is common in hospitalised older adults; compared with dementia alone it was associated with longer hospital stay, worse cognitive and functional outcomes, and higher institutionalisation and mortality.
Dementia is the leading risk factor for delirium, and hospital-, illness- and medication-related factors precipitate DSD.
Pre-existing cognitive impairment makes delirium harder to detect, and a reliable reference standard for diagnosing DSD does not yet exist.
Dementia with Lewy bodies has features of both delirium and dementia, which complicates diagnosis.
Among rapid bedside screens in older patients, two arousal tests (OSLA and RASS) had reproducibly high sensitivity and specificity; test-accuracy studies in DSD specifically were scarce.
Management of DSD includes managing distress and monitoring for resolution, with family involvement; persistent cognitive and functional decline and relapse are possible.

uncertainties: Best validated screening tool specifically for DSD.
Whether delirium exposure causes lasting neuronal injury in dementia (mechanism unclear).
mcq_angles: Features favouring delirium over dementia: onset, course and attention.
Outcomes of DSD compared with dementia alone.
Why DLB is a diagnostic mimic of delirium.
Which bedside arousal tests perform well in older inpatients.
case_hooks: 84-year-old with known Alzheimer disease admitted with UTI, now drowsy and agitated with new visual hallucinations.
Family says an elderly relative changed abruptly over two days versus a slow decline over two years.
page.gaps: Core distinguishing features (acute onset, fluctuation, inattention) are standard teaching but are not stated in the retrieved abstracts; confirm against DSM-5 or a guideline before approval.

page.mentor_intro: Agitation and other behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia are common, disabling and drive caregiver burden. Recent consensus guidance prefers person-centred non-drug approaches first and flags the serious harms of sedating drugs.

teaching_points.claim: Aggression or agitation (39%), sleep problems (38%), eating problems (36%) and irritability (32%) were the most common BPSD in acute hospital settings in a 2025 meta-analysis, and BPSD were linked to delirium, pain and psychotropic use.

Because psychotropic drugs have modest efficacy and significant adverse effects, a 2026 consensus recommends person-centred care and non-pharmacological interventions as first-line treatment for agitation.
Benefit from individualised non-drug strategies was clearest when they followed a systematic person-centred assessment of the cause of the behaviour.

A 2026 primary-care consensus advises that treatment aim to reduce patient and caregiver distress and preserve function rather than sedate, and highlights harms of off-label drugs including excess mortality, cerebrovascular events, falls and sedation.

uncertainties: Effect sizes of individual non-drug interventions (music, VR, robots) rest on small trials at risk of bias.
The drug option with the best benefit-to-harm balance for severe agitation is not settled in these sources.
mcq_angles: First-line management of agitation in dementia: assess for causes and use non-drug approaches.
Harms associated with antipsychotics in dementia.
Common hospital BPSD and their link to delirium and pain.
case_hooks: Nursing-home resident with Alzheimer disease newly shouting and resisting care; what to look for before prescribing?
Caregiver asking whether music or a sedative is better for evening agitation.
page.gaps: Drug-specific recommendations (for example antipsychotic dosing or cholinesterase inhibitors) are not in the retrieved abstracts; add from NICE or APA dementia guidance. The existing DB mentor line citing WHO digital reminiscence therapy is a weak anchor.

page.mentor_intro: Dementia with Lewy bodies is a common neurodegenerative dementia diagnosed by consensus clinical criteria supported by biomarkers; imaging with dopamine transporter SPECT and cardiac MIBG can help when the picture is uncertain.

teaching_points.claim: The fourth DLB Consortium consensus report refined recommendations for the clinical and pathological diagnosis of DLB and for management; DLB is now classified in DSM-5 as major neurocognitive disorder with Lewy bodies.

In mild cognitive impairment with Lewy bodies, attention, executive function and processing speed were worse than in MCI due to Alzheimer disease, while verbal immediate and delayed recall were better.

A 2026 Delphi consensus defines when striatal dopaminergic imaging and cardiac MIBG scintigraphy are useful in diagnosing dementia and MCI, and notes that comorbidities and medications can affect the biomarkers.

uncertainties: Consensus statements reached agreement for only about half of items in each Delphi round.
mcq_angles: Neuropsychological profile of Lewy body disease versus Alzheimer disease (attention and executive worse, recall relatively better).

page.mentor_intro: Dengue is a spectrum from self-limited febrile illness to severe plasma leakage. Recognising warning signs and secondary infection identifies who will progress, and NS1 testing is comparable to PCR in the first days of illness.

teaching_points.claim: A 2021 meta-analysis supports the WHO warning signs for predicting severe dengue and identified children, secondary infection, diabetes and renal disease as predictors; ascites, pleural effusion, hepatomegaly and melaena carried the highest odds.
Secondary dengue infection was a consistent risk factor for severe dengue in Latin America.
For acute diagnosis, pooled sensitivity was 95% for RT-PCR, 90% for NS1 ELISA (days 0-4) and 71% for IgM ELISA; IgM performs poorly early in illness, and NS1 matches RT-PCR accuracy at lower cost.
The 2025 WHO guideline provides integrated clinical management recommendations for dengue, chikungunya, Zika and yellow fever, which are hard to tell apart early without testing.

uncertainties: Individual WHO recommendations (fluids, adjunct drugs) are not in the retrieved abstract; the DB-linked WHO 2026 montelukast statement needs checking before it is used.
mcq_angles: Choice of test by day of illness: NS1/RT-PCR early, IgM later.
Warning signs and risk factors for progression to severe dengue.
Why secondary infection raises risk.

page.gaps: Phases of illness and fluid management protocol are standard teaching but are not stated in the retrieved abstracts; add from the full WHO guideline.

page.mentor_intro: Anabolic agents (teriparatide, abaloparatide, romosozumab) and denosumab raise bone density and reduce fractures more than oral bisphosphonates in selected patients; the key practical issues are sequencing, rebound after stopping denosumab, and cardiovascular safety of romosozumab.

teaching_points.claim: In osteoporosis not previously treated with bisphosphonates, teriparatide reduced fracture risk compared with bisphosphonates (RR 0.61), and teriparatide and denosumab both raised BMD more than bisphosphonates.
Romosozumab produced larger early changes in lumbar BMD and bone turnover markers than denosumab, with greater effects within 12 months.

A network meta-analysis found no significant difference in cardiovascular mortality or major cardiovascular events between romosozumab and placebo or other agents, though real-world data are still needed.
PTH1 receptor agonists reduce all fractures versus placebo, with no difference in hip fracture; abaloparatide may offer more benefit than teriparatide for non-vertebral and hip fractures.

The 2024 RACGP/Healthy Bones Australia guideline addresses FRAX-based risk stratification, rebound vertebral fractures after denosumab cessation, clarifies imminent and very high fracture risk, and supports early use of osteoanabolic therapy.

uncertainties: Cardiovascular safety of romosozumab in real-world high-risk patients.
Optimal sequencing of anabolic and antiresorptive therapy is not specified in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Major depressive disorder is treated with antidepressants, psychotherapy or both, with escalation options when response is poor. Recent syntheses refine drug choice in adolescents, show limited added value of personalised brain stimulation and pharmacogenomic panels, and leave maintenance evidence for augmentation thin.

teaching_points.claim: In adolescents, a network meta-analysis ranked escitalopram highest for functional recovery and sertraline highest for clinician-rated severity and improvement.
In children and adolescents the dose-response curve for antidepressants was relatively flat, whereas discontinuation due to adverse effects rose sharply with higher doses.
Adjunctive atypical antipsychotics differ in efficacy and acceptability in MDD, and well-controlled studies of maintenance efficacy are lacking.
Personalised (imaging-guided) repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation was not shown to be superior to fixed-target rTMS.
Pharmacogenomic-guided antidepressant selection shows a plateau in benefit with larger multigene panels, so cost-benefit and long-term remission outcomes need study.
A network meta-analysis ranked probiotics second after escitalopram and suggested possible use as adjunct or standalone therapy; this is emerging evidence rather than standard care.

uncertainties: Long-term benefit of antidepressants versus psychotherapy: few studies report follow-up after treatment ends and outcome definitions differ.
Value of augmentation with antipsychotics for maintenance.
mcq_angles: Antidepressant choice in adolescents (escitalopram, sertraline).

page.mentor_intro: De Quervain tenosynovitis is stenosing tenosynovitis of the first dorsal wrist compartment. A corticosteroid injection followed by a short period of thumb spica immobilisation is the best-supported first-line treatment, and ultrasound guidance improves results.

teaching_points.claim: A 2023 network meta-analysis supported corticosteroid injection followed by 3 to 4 weeks of immobilisation as first-line treatment; the extra benefit of adding immobilisation to injection was statistically but not clinically significant.

A 2024 network meta-analysis found corticosteroid injection with brief immobilisation remains the primary treatment, extracorporeal shockwave therapy a secondary option, and isolated non-steroid injections no substantial benefit over placebo.
Ultrasound is described as essential to achieve the best evidence-based outcomes, because first dorsal compartment anatomy varies and ultrasound detects variants accurately.
A septum dividing the first compartment and a single slip of abductor pollicis longus were more frequent in De Quervain patients than in normal cadavers.
A conservative-management review proposes a level I-II evidence treatment algorithm and notes ultrasound-guided injections are more accurate and give better outcomes.

uncertainties: Quality of trials and heterogeneity in immobilisation protocols.
mcq_angles: First-line treatment: steroid injection plus short thumb spica.
Why an intracompartmental septum predicts injection failure (anatomical variants).

page.gaps: Clinical test (Finkelstein), the tendons involved and indications for surgery are not stated in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Atopic dermatitis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease managed with emollients and topical anti-inflammatories, escalating to targeted systemic therapy (biologics and JAK inhibitors) for moderate to severe disease. Living guidelines now cover the newest agents.

teaching_points.claim: The EuroGuiDerm living guideline covers conventional immunosuppressants (azathioprine, ciclosporin, glucocorticosteroids, methotrexate, mycophenolate), biologics (dupilumab, lebrikizumab, nemolizumab, tralokinumab) and JAK inhibitors (abrocitinib, baricitinib, upadacitinib), with attention to paediatric, adolescent and pregnant patients.
The 2025 AAD focused update made strong recommendations for tapinarof cream, roflumilast cream, lebrikizumab and nemolizumab with concomitant topical therapy in adults.
Most trials of atopic dermatitis therapy are short, which limits conclusions about long-term comparative efficacy and safety.
The German-language S3 guideline Part 2 covers systemic treatment, including dupilumab, tralokinumab, JAK inhibitors, ciclosporin and systemic glucocorticoids.

uncertainties: Long-term comparative safety of biologics versus JAK inhibitors.
mcq_angles: Which classes of systemic therapy exist for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis.
Topical non-steroid options (tapinarof, roflumilast) with strong recommendation in adults.

page.mentor_intro: Device and catheter-related infections are largely preventable. Prevention bundles, ultrasound-guided insertion and antiseptic barrier caps lower risk, and paired cultures help decide whether a line must come out.

teaching_points.claim: Ultrasound-guided central venous catheter insertion significantly reduced catheter-related infection compared with landmark technique (pooled RR about 0.65), especially in experienced operators.
Antiseptic barrier caps were associated with fewer central-line bloodstream infections (RR 0.65), though most studies were of poor methodological quality.

Differential time to positivity (catheter culture growing at least 2 hours before peripheral) performs well for ruling CLABSI in or out, but is less reliable for Staphylococcus aureus (low sensitivity) and Candida (low specificity).
The 2024 ISID position paper consolidates evidence-based strategies for preventing vascular catheter infections in both high- and low-resource settings.

uncertainties: The DB topic title is 'device-related infections', which is broader than catheters (pacemakers, prosthetic joints); only catheter evidence was retrieved.

page.mentor_intro: Diabetes insipidus is either vasopressin deficiency (central) or resistance (nephrogenic). Copeptin-based testing is replacing the water deprivation test in many settings, and post-pituitary-surgery cases are usually transient.

teaching_points.claim: Congenital nephrogenic DI is caused by distal nephron insensitivity to arginine vasopressin; an international expert consensus statement now guides diagnosis and management.

After transsphenoidal surgery for pituitary adenoma permanent vasopressin deficiency was uncommon (about 2%), but prevalence reached about 30% with craniopharyngioma and 14% with Rathke cleft cyst; diagnostic criteria for post-operative DI vary.

In children with polyuria-polydipsia syndrome, stimulated copeptin showed pooled sensitivity about 0.98 and specificity about 0.95, offering a less burdensome alternative to the water deprivation test.

uncertainties: Standard protocols for copeptin testing are not yet established, particularly in children.

Exercise, metformin and their combination all improved glucose metabolism; exercise appeared superior to metformin in prediabetes whereas metformin appeared superior to exercise in established type 2 diabetes.

Risk factors for progression from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes include a high fatty liver index; moderate physical activity was protective.
A 2025 American College of Lifestyle Medicine guideline gives explicit strategies for lifestyle behaviour change for treatment and remission of type 2 diabetes and prediabetes.

page.mentor_intro: Diabetic autonomic neuropathy affects cardiovascular, gastrointestinal and other systems. Treatment options for diabetic gastroparesis are limited and trial design problems, especially high placebo response, complicate interpretation.

teaching_points.claim: Ghrelin agonists improved nausea, vomiting, early satiety and abdominal pain in diabetic gastroparesis compared with placebo, with similar adverse events.
Relamorelin showed promise in gastroparesis but headache, dizziness and gastrointestinal symptoms were more frequent in the treated group.
Placebo response in gastroparesis trials is substantial; future trials should last at least 8 weeks, use validated symptom questionnaires and distinguish gastroparesis subtypes.

Exercise may help cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy by balancing sympathetic and parasympathetic activity, though most studies were low quality and none examined older patients, poorly controlled diabetes or type 1 diabetes.
Dietary intervention may promote gastric emptying and glucose stability in diabetic gastroparesis, pending higher-quality trials.

uncertainties: Few licensed options; evidence for acupoint therapies and vitamin B12 combinations is low quality.
mcq_angles: Why gastroparesis trials show large placebo responses.
Role of glycaemic control and diet in diabetic gastroparesis.

page.mentor_intro: Diabetic foot disease needs multidisciplinary care: offloading is central to ulcer healing and recurrence prevention, and imaging and infection assessment guide osteomyelitis diagnosis.

teaching_points.claim: The IWGDF 2023 offloading guideline summarises its recommendations in a clinical pathway aimed at reducing infection, hospitalisation and amputation in people with diabetes-related foot ulcers.
After ulcer closure, reloading should include maximal offloading, especially in the first 3 months, with loading titrated by a footwear schedule.
The ACR Appropriateness Criteria (2025 update) address imaging for suspected osteomyelitis of the foot in diabetes.
A Japanese guideline weakly recommended an imaging procedure for osteomyelitis, negative-pressure wound therapy and platelet-rich plasma in diabetic foot ulcers.
A Chinese practical guideline covers metabolic control, antithrombotic and anti-infection therapy, debridement, vascular reconstruction, prevention and multidisciplinary tiered care.

uncertainties: Adjunct wound therapies (hyaluronic acid, PRP, NPWT) rest on weak recommendations or small trials.

page.mentor_intro: Diabetic ketoacidosis and the hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state are managed by a joint 2024 international consensus that updated diagnostic and resolution criteria for the first time in 15 years. SGLT2 inhibitors add a euglycaemic presentation to recognise.

teaching_points.claim: The June 2024 consensus report (ADA and partner societies) revised the criteria for diagnosis and resolution of DKA and HHS and gave new recommendations on assessment, management and prevention; the previous version was 15 years old.
Important controversies in DKA management remain unresolved because high-quality evidence is lacking.
DKA in SGLT2-inhibitor users presented with lower glucose, HbA1c, creatinine and lactate than DKA in non-users, with no difference in hospital stay, ICU admission or in-hospital mortality.
Perioperative SGLT2-inhibitor guidance includes monitoring and prevention strategies for euglycaemic diabetic ketoacidosis.

uncertainties: Optimal fluid type and rate, insulin regimen and potassium strategy are listed as controversial in the review but not specified in the retrieved abstract.

Updated diagnostic and resolution criteria in the 2024 consensus.

page.mentor_intro: Diabetic kidney disease is found by routine eGFR and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio screening, and outcomes depend on starting and sustaining guideline-directed therapy. Real-world data show the biggest gap is in screening, not prescribing.

teaching_points.claim: Early detection with routine eGFR and UACR, followed by timely and sustained guideline-directed medical therapy together with lifestyle change, is described as the most effective strategy to alter the natural history of DKD.

In a real-world analysis, gaps in guideline-concordant DKD care were driven mainly by screening deficiencies rather than treatment failures, and care varied more by healthcare setting than by patient characteristics.
A Thai real-world study found real-world implementation of guideline-directed therapy in DKD remains inadequate, with a call for regular review and feedback.
A UK joint ABCD and UKKA guideline provides practical lipid-management recommendations for adults with DKD.
A 2026 consensus guidance for DKD includes finerenone alongside lifestyle and dietary measures and stresses affordability and patient education.

uncertainties: The four drug classes and their sequencing are not named in the retrieved abstracts.
mcq_angles: Screening for DKD: eGFR plus UACR, repeated in all people with diabetes.
Why implementation, not drug availability, limits outcomes.
case_hooks: Type 2 diabetic with UACR 120 mg/g and eGFR 55: which therapies to start?
page.gaps: UACR stage thresholds, RAS blockade titration, SGLT2 inhibitor and finerenone indications are standard KDIGO/ADA content but are not stated in the abstracts retrieved; add from KDIGO 2022 diabetes in CKD guideline.

page.mentor_intro: Painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy is common and under-detected. Risk rises with diabetes duration and nephropathy, systematic screening is advised, and a few non-drug options show benefit in refractory pain.

teaching_points.claim: Risk factors for painful diabetic neuropathy include longer diabetes duration (OR 1.05) and nephropathy (OR 1.32); the authors call for targeted screening and standardised diagnostic tools.
A broader meta-analysis lists retinopathy, nephropathy, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, smoking, alcohol, obesity and age at onset among risk factors for painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
Spinal cord stimulation produced significant pain reduction and quality-of-life gains in painful diabetic neuropathy and outperformed conventional medical therapy.
Vitamin D supplementation may reduce short-term pain, but small, low-quality trials mean routine testing or supplementation cannot yet be recommended.
Patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy and type 2 diabetes had lower lower-limb muscle strength than those without neuropathy.
A GCC Delphi consensus recommends systematic screening, early multimodal management and better access to guideline-recommended therapies.

uncertainties: Acupuncture may reduce pain versus sham but evidence quality is limited.
mcq_angles: Risk factors for painful diabetic neuropathy.
Role of spinal cord stimulation for refractory pain.
case_hooks: Burning feet at night in a 10-year type 2 diabetic: screening and first-line analgesia.
page.gaps: First-line drug classes (duloxetine, pregabalin/gabapentin, tricyclics), monofilament screening and foot-care advice are not in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: For vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy and diabetic macular oedema, intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy is now the first-line option over panretinal photocoagulation, with steroid implants, laser and newer agents used for non-responders.

teaching_points.claim: In a network meta-analysis anti-VEGF therapy was more effective than panretinal photocoagulation for visual acuity, macular thickness and neovascularisation with a better safety profile, supporting anti-VEGF as first-line for vision-threatening DR.

Treatment beyond metabolic control comprises intravitreal anti-VEGF or corticosteroids, laser photocoagulation and vitreous surgery; screening is essential because early disease is often asymptomatic.
For DME, anti-VEGF monotherapy and anti-VEGF plus laser or intravitreal steroid had comparable effects; adding intravitreal steroid gave no significant benefit.
Switching to faricimab for persistent DME after prior anti-VEGF produced anatomical and functional improvement and lengthened treatment intervals by about 1.5 weeks.
An early switch to intravitreal dexamethasone implant after failed anti-VEGF tended to give better outcomes than a late switch, though heterogeneity limits the evidence.
Deep-learning fundus photograph screening showed high discriminative performance in prospective real-world settings.

uncertainties: Best combination or switching strategy in treatment-resistant DME.
mcq_angles: First-line therapy for centre-involving DME or high-risk PDR: anti-VEGF.

page.mentor_intro: For vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy and diabetic macular oedema, intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy is now the first-line option over panretinal photocoagulation, with steroid implants, laser and newer agents used for non-responders.

teaching_points.claim: In a network meta-analysis anti-VEGF therapy was more effective than panretinal photocoagulation for visual acuity, macular thickness and neovascularisation with a better safety profile, supporting anti-VEGF as first-line for vision-threatening DR.

Treatment beyond metabolic control comprises intravitreal anti-VEGF or corticosteroids, laser photocoagulation and vitreous surgery; screening is essential because early disease is often asymptomatic.
For DME, anti-VEGF monotherapy and anti-VEGF plus laser or intravitreal steroid had comparable effects; adding intravitreal steroid gave no significant benefit.
Switching to faricimab for persistent DME after prior anti-VEGF produced anatomical and functional improvement and lengthened treatment intervals by about 1.5 weeks.
An early switch to intravitreal dexamethasone implant after failed anti-VEGF tended to give better outcomes than a late switch, though heterogeneity limits the evidence.

page.mentor_intro: Diffuse alveolar haemorrhage is a life-threatening pulmonary syndrome of immune or other causes. Management is treatment of the cause with high-dose immunosuppression, with extracorporeal support available in refractory cases.

teaching_points.claim: In granulomatosis with polyangiitis presenting with DAH, steroids, rituximab and cyclophosphamide are first-line treatment, plasmapheresis is still used, and ECMO can be salvage therapy.

In SLE, the need for plasmapheresis and mechanical ventilation marked poor outcome, and antiphospholipid antibody positivity (especially lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin IgG) increased DAH risk.

Antiphospholipid-syndrome DAH carries estimated mortality of 30.3% at one year and 45.8% at five years, with worse outcomes with triple positivity, thrombocytopenia, valvular involvement and catastrophic APS.
Levamisole-adulterated cocaine can cause ANCA-associated pulmonary-renal syndrome; asking about cocaine use is required for diagnosis and counselling.
In a systematic review of extracorporeal life support for diffuse alveolar damage or haemorrhage, 30-day mortality was 10.5% with no difference between VA and VV ECMO.

uncertainties: No randomised trials guide treatment of SLE- or APS-associated DAH.

page.mentor_intro: Relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is now treated with CAR T-cell therapy in second line for eligible patients, and CD3xCD20 bispecific antibodies are changing practice in later relapse and are being tested earlier.

teaching_points.claim: The British Society for Haematology guideline recommends CAR T-cell therapy or a CD3xCD20 bispecific antibody at second relapse in eligible patients, with specific advice on immunohistochemistry, bendamustine use and bridging to CAR T.
NCCN 2025 insights report that adding CD3xCD20 bispecific antibodies to chemoimmunotherapy improves outcomes in relapsed/refractory DLBCL.

A meta-analysis of second-line anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy found higher response rates and delayed progression versus standard of care, with progression-free survival benefit for liso-cel (HR 0.37) and axi-cel (HR 0.42) compared with tisa-cel.
PET/CT is proposed as a central biomarker for early identification of high-risk patients so that CAR T referral is not delayed.
The SEOM-GOTEL 2025 guideline notes bispecifics may challenge R-CHOP as the benchmark for newly diagnosed DLBCL.

After CAR T failure, treatment choice depends on performance status, whether disease is localised or systemic and prior therapy; loncastuximab tesirine showed meaningful activity, including post-CAR T, with frequent but manageable cytopenias.

uncertainties: Sequencing of CAR T and bispecifics; heterogeneity of real-world loncastuximab data.
mcq_angles: Second-line therapy in early-relapsing DLBCL: CAR T versus autologous transplant.
Role of bispecific antibodies after CAR T.
case_hooks: 62-year-old with DLBCL relapsing 8 months after R-CHOP: next step and role of PET.
page.gaps: Frontline R-CHOP and Pola-R-CHP data, prognostic indices (IPI), CAR T toxicities (CRS, ICANS) are not in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: DLCO measures gas transfer across the alveolar-capillary membrane and must be interpreted with spirometry, lung volumes and clinical context, taking test variability into account. It tracks severity and prognosis in COPD and recovery after lung injury.

teaching_points.claim: The ERS/ATS technical standard states that interpretation of lung function tests must be complemented by clinical expertise and consideration of the test's biological variability and uncertainty.
In COPD, DLCO relates to disease severity, exacerbation risk, mortality, emphysema predominance and presence of pulmonary hypertension, because it reflects ventilation and perfusion together.
Four months after critical COVID-19, reduced DLCO was the main finding; risk rose with age over 60, mechanical ventilation and longer ICU stay.
Lung volume reduction in emphysema improved DLCO by a mean of 5.7% predicted, with no real change in blood gases, plausibly through better V/Q matching.
DLCO and DLCO/VA are heritable traits, and a functional variant in ADGRG6 was associated with DLCO/VA.
The ATS recommends standardised formats for pulmonary function reports, including test quality assessment.
A chest-medicine review outlines a clinically friendly approach to DLCO interpretation and the scenarios where it helps most.

uncertainties: The abstracts do not list conditions with high DLCO or the haemoglobin correction.
mcq_angles: Low DLCO in emphysema and interstitial disease with preserved or restrictive spirometry.
DLCO follow-up after severe COVID-19.
case_hooks: Breathless smoker with obstructive spirometry and markedly low DLCO.
page.gaps: Conditions causing raised DLCO (alveolar haemorrhage, polycythaemia), anaemia and carboxyhaemoglobin corrections, and KCO interpretation are standard teaching but not stated in the retrieved abstracts.

Clinical care of family members of DCM patients is moving to integrate genotype-phenotype knowledge, with open questions in risk prediction and early detection.
In genotype-positive DCM there is a persistent male excess even though genetic risk is equally prevalent, suggesting additional drivers of sex-biased penetrance.
Inflammatory cardiomyopathy requires lifelong follow-up because of persistence, arrhythmic burden and recurrence of inflammatory hot phases.

The ISTH guidance reviews specific and non-specific reversal agents and states when reversal is indicated.
A clinical guideline on DOAC reversal in life-threatening bleeding could make no recommendation for recombinant factor VIIa as a non-specific haemostatic agent because of scant data.
A DOAC dipstick algorithm allows rapid exclusion of clinically relevant drug levels and distinguishes factor Xa from thrombin inhibitors where quantitative assays are unavailable.
The ACCP perioperative guideline notes that uncertainty remains about best practice for most perioperative antithrombotic questions.
In cirrhosis, anticoagulation is recommended for symptomatic portal vein thrombosis and suggested for asymptomatic progressing thrombosis.

page.mentor_intro: Disseminated intravascular coagulation mortality is very high but varies by underlying disease and diagnostic criteria. Recent Japanese guidelines provide disease-specific recommendations and weak recommendations for certain therapies.

teaching_points.claim: A systematic review found DIC mortality very high but heterogeneous depending on underlying disease and diagnostic criteria, with no clear yearly improvement.
In haematologic malignancy, recombinant thrombomodulin is weakly recommended (Grade 2B), while heparin and serine protease inhibitors are weakly not recommended (Grade 2C).

For sepsis-associated DIC, the Japanese guidelines made no recommendation on heparin or serine protease inhibitors because of lack of evidence, and listed combination use of antithrombin and recombinant thrombomodulin as a research question.
For trauma, burn and obstetric DIC, the guidelines provide stratified recommendations including fibrinogen, antithrombin and tranexamic acid.
Global surveys show major gaps between recommended and real-world DIC practice, especially in resource-limited settings.

uncertainties: Whether DIC is present and clinically relevant in cirrhosis remains unresolved.

teaching_points.claim: A systematic review found DIC mortality very high but heterogeneous depending on underlying disease and diagnostic criteria, with no clear yearly improvement.
In haematologic malignancy, recombinant thrombomodulin is weakly recommended (Grade 2B), while heparin and serine protease inhibitors are weakly not recommended (Grade 2C).

For sepsis-associated DIC, the Japanese guidelines made no recommendation on heparin or serine protease inhibitors because of lack of evidence, and listed combination use of antithrombin and recombinant thrombomodulin as a research question.
For trauma, burn and obstetric DIC, the guidelines provide stratified recommendations including fibrinogen, antithrombin and tranexamic acid.
Global surveys show major gaps between recommended and real-world DIC practice, especially in resource-limited settings.

uncertainties: Whether DIC is present and clinically relevant in cirrhosis remains unresolved.
mcq_angles: Treat the underlying cause as the cornerstone of DIC management.
Disease-specific differences in anticoagulant benefit.
case_hooks: Septic patient with falling platelets, prolonged PT and raised D-dimer.
page.gaps: ISTH scoring system components and transfusion thresholds are not in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Distributive shock is managed with fluids and norepinephrine, with vasopressin as the usual second agent and angiotensin II as an option in refractory cases; anaphylactic shock is a distinct adrenaline-dependent form.

teaching_points.claim: The Canadian Critical Care Society suggests vasopressin or analogues added to catecholamines over catecholamines alone for distributive shock (conditional recommendation, low-certainty evidence).

A network meta-analysis in septic shock found norepinephrine plus dobutamine associated with lower 28-day mortality and dopamine with higher mortality than norepinephrine, terlipressin or vasopressin.
Angiotensin II allowed significant reduction of adjunctive vasopressors at 3 hours without increased adverse events, and expert consensus calls for more trials in refractory vasodilatory shock.
A meta-analysis of non-adrenergic vasopressors found confidence intervals compatible with both no effect and clinically important benefit, justifying further RCTs.
Vasoplegic syndrome during heart transplantation lacks a formal definition, and studies of refractory cases are needed.

uncertainties: Mortality benefit of second-line vasopressors beyond catecholamine sparing.
mcq_angles: Add vasopressin to norepinephrine in refractory septic shock.
Dopamine's higher mortality in septic shock.

page.mentor_intro: Diuretic resistance is poorly defined; appropriately high intravenous loop diuretic doses usually overcome it, and the goal is decongestion rather than protecting a creatinine value. Evidence comes largely from acute heart failure rather than ICU populations.

teaching_points.claim: Diuretic resistance is not accurately defined in acute heart failure and is uncommon with appropriately high IV loop diuretic doses; the aim should be decongestion rather than over-emphasising mild kidney biomarker changes.
Metolazone was as effective as chlorothiazide as an add-on to loop diuretics in acute decompensated heart failure, with comparable adverse events.

Combination diuretic strategies improved early decongestion without affecting prognosis, and SGLT2 inhibitor use during admission was associated with lower all-cause mortality and heart failure events.
Urinary sodium-guided diuretic therapy increased natriuresis and diuresis without more adverse events but had no proven effect on mortality, rehospitalisation or renal outcomes.

uncertainties: Optimal add-on agent; applicability of AHF data to ICU patients.
mcq_angles: Add a thiazide-type diuretic to a loop diuretic for resistance.
Using spot urinary sodium to judge diuretic response.
case_hooks: ICU patient on high-dose furosemide with persistent oliguria and fluid overload.
page.gaps: ICU-specific evidence (renal replacement, ultrafiltration, albumin) is not in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Uncomplicated left-sided diverticulitis can often be managed without antibiotics in selected patients, while surgery decisions for recurrent or complicated disease are individualised.

teaching_points.claim: The ACP suggests initially managing select patients with acute uncomplicated left-sided diverticulitis without antibiotics (conditional recommendation, low-certainty evidence).
For persistent, frequently recurring or complicated diverticulitis, the decision for elective surgery should be personalised after discussing benefits, harms, costs and patient preferences.

The 2025 EAES rapid guideline and the 2026 Fiesole global consensus provide current recommendations on surgical management of complicated diverticulitis and on diagnosis, management and prevention across health systems.
German guidelines separately cover pathogenesis and classification (Part I) and conservative, interventional and surgical management (Part II).
The 2024 IDSA update on complicated intra-abdominal infection includes diagnostic and antimicrobial recommendations.

uncertainties: Long-term outcomes of selective antibiotic use and surgical strategies are named research priorities.
mcq_angles: Antibiotics are not always required in uncomplicated diverticulitis.
Elective colectomy decisions after recurrence are individualised.
case_hooks: 45-year-old with left iliac fossa pain, CT-confirmed uncomplicated diverticulitis, no systemic upset.

page.mentor_intro: DNACPR and treatment escalation decisions belong inside advance care planning: patient-centred, balancing beneficence and autonomy, and carried through the perioperative period. Retrieved evidence is general rather than UK-statute specific.

teaching_points.claim: The ERC 2025 ethics guidelines emphasise a patient-centred approach and the balance between beneficence and autonomy in resuscitation decisions.
AAGBI/AoA guidance states perioperative implementation of advance care plans, including CPR plans, applies to all procedures however minor and regardless of anaesthetic technique.
A meta-analysis of RCTs in advanced cancer evaluated advance care planning; effects on dignity and care concordance need validation and optimal timing is unclear.
Asking patients to talk to their proxy or family about quality versus quantity of life can help initiate advance care planning.
Dyadic (patient and caregiver) advance care planning has been assessed for effect on end-of-life communication and decision-making, with barriers still to be defined.

uncertainties: Best timing and format of advance care planning.
mcq_angles: A DNACPR decision is not a decision to withhold other treatment.
Perioperative handling of an existing CPR plan.

page.mentor_intro: Direct oral anticoagulants are used without routine monitoring; the decisions that matter are perioperative interruption without bridging, specific reversal in life-threatening bleeding, and safe testing of drug levels.

teaching_points.claim: The 2025 DOAC guidance states DOACs can be interrupted and resumed for procedures without bridging with LMWH, and names specific reversal agents for factor Xa inhibitors and idarucizumab for dabigatran, with prothrombin complex concentrates if these are unavailable.
The ISTH guidance reviews specific and non-specific reversal agents and states when reversal is indicated.
A clinical guideline on DOAC reversal in life-threatening bleeding could make no recommendation for recombinant factor VIIa as a non-specific haemostatic agent because of scant data.
A DOAC dipstick algorithm allows rapid exclusion of clinically relevant drug levels and distinguishes factor Xa from thrombin inhibitors where quantitative assays are unavailable.
The ACCP perioperative guideline notes that uncertainty remains about best practice for most perioperative antithrombotic questions.
In cirrhosis, anticoagulation is recommended for symptomatic portal vein thrombosis and suggested for asymptomatic progressing thrombosis.

uncertainties: Evidence for non-specific haemostatic agents is limited.
mcq_angles: Reversal agent for dabigatran (idarucizumab) versus factor Xa inhibitors.
Why bridging is not needed for DOAC interruption.

page.gaps: Dosing, renal adjustment and drug-drug interactions for each DOAC are not in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions are medical emergencies. Retrieved evidence concerns SJS/TEN, where early diagnosis, drug withdrawal, supportive care and monitoring for infection are central; DRESS-specific evidence was not retrieved.

teaching_points.claim: The German S3 guideline on epidermal necrolysis covers diagnosis, initial management and immunomodulating systemic therapy in Part 1, and supportive care and outpatient follow-up in Part 2.
Non-SCORTEN predictors of mortality in adult SJS/TEN include pre-existing renal disease, renal and respiratory involvement, diabetes, sepsis, comorbidities and time to hospitalisation.
Infectious complications are frequent in adult SJS/TEN and clinicians should monitor for and promptly investigate them during hospitalisation.
Cotrimoxazole-induced SCARs are associated with multiple HLA alleles, including HLA-A*11:01, HLA-B*13:01, HLA-B*15:02, HLA-B*38:02 and HLA-C*08:01.
Paediatric SJS/TEN guidelines are heterogeneous: supportive care is emphasised but pharmacologic and long-term guidance is inconsistent.

uncertainties: Evidence for any specific immunomodulatory drug in SJS/TEN is limited and guideline-dependent.
mcq_angles: Stop the culprit drug immediately in SJS/TEN.
HLA-B*15:02 and carbamazepine-type pharmacogenomic screening logic.
case_hooks: Two weeks after starting an antiepileptic, a patient develops fever, mucosal erosions and blistering skin.

page.mentor_intro: Most patients labelled penicillin-allergic are not allergic. Delabelling by direct oral challenge or structured testing is safe, can be done by non-allergists, and improves antibiotic choice.

teaching_points.claim: Penicillin allergy delabelling by non-allergists is efficacious and safe, with reported harm about 0% (95% CI 0-1%); the proportion delabelled rises with the complexity of testing, but many can be delabelled without skin testing.
Reactions to direct penicillin challenges are infrequent and comparable to indirect challenges after allergy testing, so direct challenge is safe across age groups and settings.
BSACI guidance supports delabelling services run by non-allergists for low-risk patients with a framework for drug provocation testing, with separate adult and paediatric sections.
Inaccurate allergy labels should be removed after a negative drug provocation test with proper counselling.
Surgical patients with a penicillin allergy label can be assessed and tested by trained professionals meeting minimum safe-testing standards.
The reported global prevalence of penicillin allergy comes mainly from high-income countries and secondary care.

uncertainties: Data from low-income settings.
mcq_angles: Direct oral amoxicillin challenge for low-risk histories.
Why delabelling improves antimicrobial stewardship.
case_hooks: Patient with childhood rash on amoxicillin needing perioperative cefazolin.

page.mentor_intro: Drug-induced acute interstitial nephritis is an under-recognised cause of acute kidney injury with several common culprits (PPIs, beta-lactams, 5-ASA, immune checkpoint inhibitors). Stopping the drug and, in selected cases, giving steroids is the mainstay.

teaching_points.claim: Proton pump inhibitor use was associated with adverse kidney outcomes including AIN (RR 3.61), though from low-quality observational data.
AIN is the most common cause of immune checkpoint inhibitor-related kidney injury and is often treated with steroids; the need for biopsy is controversial.

French shared guidelines for ICI-associated AKI vary steroid treatment with severity and renal response, note a lack of strong data for steroid-resistant cases, and discuss rechallenge, which appears to carry a good renal prognosis.
In 5-ASA-induced interstitial nephritis in IBD, at least six-monthly monitoring of renal function is suggested because early steroid treatment may be beneficial.
Vedolizumab can rarely cause AIN in IBD, so symptoms and laboratory findings consistent with AIN warrant monitoring of kidney function.
Cefazolin is a first-line option for MSSA infections, with fewer discontinuations for side effects than antistaphylococcal penicillins.

uncertainties: Role of biopsy and steroid duration in AIN.
mcq_angles: Common drug causes of AIN: PPI, beta-lactams, NSAIDs, 5-ASA, ICIs.

Immune checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis needs enhanced recognition and timely individualised management.
JAK inhibitors increased non-opportunistic respiratory infections versus placebo, but the risk of serious pulmonary adverse events was low.

page.mentor_intro: Many common drugs (antidepressants, antibiotics, antipsychotics, antimalarials, some cancer drugs) prolong the QT interval. Risk is managed by identifying high-risk patients, avoiding interacting combinations and monitoring ECGs.

teaching_points.claim: The 2023 Canadian Cardiovascular Society update notes that certain beta-blockers are highly effective in long QT, defibrillators are infrequently required, and that many commonly prescribed drugs such as antidepressants and antibiotics prolong QT, with recommendations for their safe use.
Short courses of chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine in COVID-19 caused significant QT prolongation, and daily ECG monitoring and other mitigation were advised.
A later meta-analysis found that despite being listed as QT-prolonging, hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine did not increase major adverse cardiac events.
Among CDK4/6 inhibitors, ribociclib prolonged QTc about twice as much as the others and grade 3 prolongations occurred exclusively with ribociclib.
QT-prolonging drug-drug interactions are common in psychiatric prescribing, so precautionary safety interventions and vigilance are advised.
In acute antipsychotic poisoning, QT risk depends on the drug and dose ingested, time since ingestion, heart rate and co-ingestions, and the evidence quality is heterogeneous.

uncertainties: Whether QT prolongation by hydroxychloroquine translates into clinical events.
mcq_angles: Risk-factor combination for torsades: female sex, hypokalaemia, bradycardia, multiple QT drugs.
Ribociclib versus other CDK4/6 inhibitors.
case_hooks: Patient started on a macrolide while taking citalopram, with QTc 520 ms.
page.gaps: Electrolyte correction, magnesium for torsades, QTc thresholds and the formula for correction are not in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions are medical emergencies. Retrieved evidence concerns SJS/TEN, where early diagnosis, drug withdrawal, supportive care and monitoring for infection are central; DRESS-specific evidence was not retrieved.

teaching_points.claim: The German S3 guideline on epidermal necrolysis covers diagnosis, initial management and immunomodulating systemic therapy in Part 1, and supportive care and outpatient follow-up in Part 2.
Non-SCORTEN predictors of mortality in adult SJS/TEN include pre-existing renal disease, renal and respiratory involvement, diabetes, sepsis, comorbidities and time to hospitalisation.
Infectious complications are frequent in adult SJS/TEN and clinicians should monitor for and promptly investigate them during hospitalisation.
Cotrimoxazole-induced SCARs are associated with multiple HLA alleles, including HLA-A*11:01, HLA-B*13:01, HLA-B*15:02, HLA-B*38:02 and HLA-C*08:01.
Paediatric SJS/TEN guidelines are heterogeneous: supportive care is emphasised but pharmacologic and long-term guidance is inconsistent.

uncertainties: Evidence for any specific immunomodulatory drug in SJS/TEN is limited and guideline-dependent.
mcq_angles: Stop the culprit drug immediately in SJS/TEN.
HLA-B*15:02 and carbamazepine-type pharmacogenomic screening logic.
case_hooks: Two weeks after starting an antiepileptic, a patient develops fever, mucosal erosions and blistering skin.
page.gaps: DRESS (RegiSCAR criteria, eosinophilia, steroid use, long latency) and benign drug eruptions are not covered by the retrieved abstracts; topics 568, 576 and 577 need a DRESS source before approval.

page.mentor_intro: Epilepsy is drug-resistant when seizures persist after adequate trials of two appropriate drugs; resective surgery and neuromodulation are the options, and they may also lower mortality.

teaching_points.claim: A meta-analysis found 46% of patients with drug-resistant epilepsy had at least 50% seizure reduction with vagus nerve stimulation, and VNS should be considered when antiseizure medication has failed.
In long-term comparisons, responsive neurostimulation and deep brain stimulation outperformed invasive VNS; transcutaneous methods showed promise but need confirmation.
Epilepsy surgery and neuromodulation may reduce overall mortality including SUDEP, but dedicated long-term prospective studies are needed.
Transcutaneous auricular VNS is under study as an adjunct, but methodological concerns mean well-designed RCTs are needed.
A consensus on ring chromosome 20 syndrome says ketogenic diet, VNS or deep brain stimulation can be considered for drug-resistant epilepsy.

uncertainties: Which patients benefit most from each neuromodulation modality.
mcq_angles: Definition of drug-resistant epilepsy and referral to an epilepsy surgery centre.

page.mentor_intro: Drug-resistant TB treatment has moved to shorter, all-oral regimens built on bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid (BPaL/BPaLM), replacing injectable-containing, long regimens in eligible patients.

teaching_points.claim: The ATS/CDC/ERS/IDSA 2025 update recommends novel drug-resistant TB regimens containing bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid with or without moxifloxacin, and all-oral shorter regimens for eligible individuals.
The WHO 2022 module groups drug-resistant TB recommendations in one document, and the 2023 update has been described as a turning point to shorter, all-oral, patient-centred MDR/RR-TB care.
The Spanish guideline recommends a six-month regimen (conditioned by fluoroquinolone resistance) for pulmonary MDR-TB, plus directly observed or video-observed treatment.
Austrian consensus states BPaLM (and BPaL) may be used for MDR, pre-XDR and rifampicin-resistant TB if prerequisites are met.
Pre-XDR and XDR burden among patients with MDR-TB is considerable, supporting drug-resistance surveillance.

uncertainties: Implementation challenges of new regimens in low-resource settings.

page.mentor_intro: After PCI for acute coronary syndrome, shortening dual antiplatelet therapy and continuing a potent P2Y12 inhibitor alone reduces bleeding without more ischaemic events, particularly with ticagrelor.

teaching_points.claim: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after short DAPT in ACS halved bleeding without increasing ischaemic events; ticagrelor, but not clopidogrel, monotherapy reduced MACE, net adverse clinical events and mortality versus standard DAPT.

In a network meta-analysis, short DAPT followed by potent P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy ranked best to reduce MACCE after drug-eluting stents in ACS; the safety of stopping aspirin in clopidogrel-treated patients remained unclear.
Adding a PPI to DAPT significantly lowered upper gastrointestinal bleeding and all-cause mortality without harming major cardiovascular outcomes.
A 2026 network meta-analysis suggested aspirin discontinuation may be optimal for women and switching the P2Y12 inhibitor to clopidogrel for men; this sex-difference signal needs confirmation.
The 2025 ACC/AHA ACS guideline updates many prior recommendations with new evidence.
The ESC consensus on antithrombotic therapy after CABG reviews the evidence and gives statements for best practice.

uncertainties: Optimal de-escalation strategy by sex and bleeding risk.

page.mentor_intro: Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophies need multidisciplinary standards of care covering corticosteroids, cardiac surveillance and treatment, respiratory and orthopaedic care, transition to adult services and now gene therapy.

teaching_points.claim: A French guideline addresses choice of corticosteroid, dose and management of long-term side effects in DMD, including osteoporosis, growth and pubertal delay, weight gain, cataract, hypertension, behavioural disorders, vaccines and metabolic complications.
The ACTION committee consensus sets a standardised framework for cardiac care in DMD to improve cardiac prognosis.
French Becker muscular dystrophy guidelines cover neurological, respiratory, cardiac and orthopaedic follow-up and include cardiac management for female carriers.
The 2022 HRS consensus addresses evaluation and management of arrhythmic risk in neuromuscular disorders.
Consensus recommendations exist for delivery and monitoring of gene therapy in DMD, based on limited rather than well-established evidence.
International Delphi statements and the Adult North Star Network guideline support transition from paediatric to adult care and adult standards of care.

uncertainties: Long-term benefit and risk of gene therapy.
mcq_angles: Cardiomyopathy surveillance in DMD and female carriers.
Steroid side-effect management in boys with DMD.
case_hooks: 8-year-old boy with calf pseudohypertrophy, Gowers sign and raised creatine kinase.
page.gaps: Dystrophin gene mutation classes (reading-frame rule) and exon-skipping therapy are not covered by the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Dupilumab blocks IL-4/IL-13 signalling and treats atopic dermatitis and other type 2 diseases. Key safety points are conjunctivitis and the possibility of unmasking cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

teaching_points.claim: Dupilumab may unmask or exacerbate cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, particularly mycosis fungoides and Sezary syndrome, and expert consensus advises reassessment when disease worsens or atypical features emerge, discouraging a switch to other Th2-targeting biologics.
In chronic hand eczema dupilumab showed efficacy; adverse effects included conjunctivitis (9.9%), herpes viral infection (1.4%) and facial erythema or dermatitis (1.3%).
The 2026 AAD paediatric atopic dermatitis guideline strongly recommends against systemic corticosteroids and conditionally recommends against topical antimicrobials and PUVA phototherapy.
A multidisciplinary Delphi consensus reached agreement on all statements about definition, diagnosis and management of moderate-severe paediatric atopic dermatitis.
Dupilumab improved quality of life in atopic dermatitis in a meta-analysis of randomised trials.

uncertainties: Lymphoma risk profile and patient selection need prospective study.
mcq_angles: Conjunctivitis as the commonest dupilumab adverse effect.
Atypical or worsening eczema on dupilumab: think CTCL.
case_hooks: Adult on dupilumab with worsening plaques and new lymphadenopathy.
page.gaps: Mechanism details and approved indications beyond atopic dermatitis (asthma, CRSwNP, eosinophilic oesophagitis, prurigo) are not in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Durable LVAD therapy improves survival in advanced heart failure, and guideline-directed medical therapy after implant is associated with better outcomes yet is under-used.

teaching_points.claim: In an international multicentre study GDMT in LVAD patients was associated with improved survival, even with single-agent therapy, but only 30% received optimal triple therapy.
GDMT within 3 months of LVAD implant was associated with fewer all-cause readmissions and a non-significant trend to lower 12-month mortality.
Advancing age is associated with lower GDMT use in HeartMate 3 recipients, but other patient factors do not explain low prescribing.
Ventricular arrhythmias are frequent after LVAD implantation and are associated with higher all-cause mortality, particularly when early.
British societies have issued a guideline on managing emergencies in implantable LVAD recipients, including resuscitation.
An AHA scientific statement covers kidney dysfunction in advanced heart failure, including LVAD and transplant and palliative-care decisions.

uncertainties: Optimal GDMT regimen and timing after implant.
mcq_angles: Arrhythmia burden after LVAD.
GDMT remains indicated after LVAD.

page.mentor_intro: The 2026 US dyslipidaemia guideline widens statin eligibility for primary prevention, while AACE guidance centres on ASCVD risk, individualised drug choice and shared decision-making. For patients who cannot reach LDL-C goals on statins, alternative strategies give comparable outcomes.

teaching_points.claim: The 2026 ACC/AHA multi-society guideline addresses evaluation, management and monitoring of high cholesterol, hypertriglyceridaemia and elevated lipoprotein(a).
An analysis found the 2026 guideline substantially expands the US population recommended for primary-prevention statin therapy, predominantly among lower-risk individuals.
The 2025 AACE pharmacologic guideline offers effective and safe options for adults with or at increased risk of ASCVD who need additional lipid-lowering medication, with shared decision-making.
The 2025 AACE algorithm emphasises ASCVD risk assessment, pancreatitis risk, individualised pharmacotherapy, cost-effectiveness and health equity.

In ASCVD, an alternative LDL-lowering strategy (instead of high-intensity statin alone) had comparable 3-year efficacy for death or cardiovascular events with lower LDL-C, less new-onset diabetes and less intolerance.

uncertainties: Net benefit of expanded primary-prevention statin eligibility in low-risk people.
mcq_angles: Add-on options when LDL-C remains above goal on maximal statin.
Lipoprotein(a) as a risk enhancer.
case_hooks: Post-MI patient with LDL-C 2.4 mmol/L on high-intensity atorvastatin.

page.mentor_intro: Uninvestigated dyspepsia without alarm features is managed by H. pylori test-and-treat and acid suppression; functional dyspepsia is diagnosed after exclusion and treated stepwise.

teaching_points.claim: The ACG/CAG guideline advises H. pylori eradication in infected patients with functional dyspepsia, then PPI, tricyclic antidepressant and prokinetic therapy in that order for non-responders or H. pylori-negative patients, and does not recommend routine GI motility testing.
The Italian functional dyspepsia guideline found insufficient evidence to recommend complementary and alternative treatments.
Korea's 2025 H. pylori guideline establishes quadruple therapies as the new standard via empirical treatment or PCR-guided tailored therapy, with P-CABs and bismuth-based regimens as key components.
Japan's 2024 revised guideline covers H. pylori management and gastric cancer prevention.
The ACG 2025 guideline covers diagnosis and management of gastric premalignant conditions and identifies research needs for defining high-risk populations.

uncertainties: Regional antibiotic resistance drives regimen choice.

teaching_points.claim: ASCO guideline updates address adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors, including abemaciclib with endocrine therapy for high-risk early breast cancer.

A patient-level meta-analysis of 12 randomised trials found extended aromatase inhibitor therapy reduced distant recurrence by about a quarter despite substantial non-adherence; mortality effects need longer follow-up.
Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitors plus chemotherapy have a manageable safety profile, but no benefit was observed with adjuvant checkpoint inhibitors; patient selection is a research priority.
Consensus guidance stresses dose intensity, adherence and early reporting of adverse effects for CDK4/6 inhibitors.
A follow-up consensus emphasises surveillance for treatment toxicities, quality of life and lifestyle measures after early breast cancer.

uncertainties: Who benefits from extended endocrine therapy and from checkpoint inhibitors.

teaching_points.claim: The 2001 Rivers trial concluded that early goal-directed therapy provides significant outcome benefits in severe sepsis and septic shock.

ProMISe found that, after adequate fluid resuscitation, management by a strict EGDT protocol did not improve outcome.
The Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 guidelines provide current international recommendations for management of sepsis and septic shock.

page.mentor_intro: Refeeding syndrome, with hypophosphataemia as its marker, is the main medical hazard when re-nourishing severely malnourished patients, including those with anorexia nervosa. Risk identification, cautious feeding and electrolyte replacement are the cornerstones.

teaching_points.claim: Australasian (ASPEN) consensus statements aim to improve identification and management of refeeding syndrome and risk, including electrolyte replacement considerations and route.
A Spanish eating-disorders consensus says refeeding syndrome must be prevented during renourishment and that anorexia nervosa in pregnancy, vegetarianism or type 1 diabetes needs specific care.

In hospitalised adolescents with anorexia nervosa, research is needed to define risk factors for refeeding hypophosphataemia and optimal delivery (oral versus enteral), macronutrient content and electrolyte replacement.
A systematic review of adult refeeding risk factors found too few high-quality studies to confirm individual factors for risk-prediction tools.
An umbrella review advises considering phosphate testing in high-risk scenarios and following evidence-based supplementation guidelines.

uncertainties: Optimal starting calorie level and risk-prediction rules.
mcq_angles: Biochemical hallmark of refeeding syndrome: low phosphate, potassium and magnesium; thiamine.
High-risk patients for refeeding.

page.mentor_intro: Ebola disease still carries high case fatality, and monoclonal antibody therapy (REGN-EB3 or mAb114 as Inmazeb or Ebanga) plus optimised supportive care is the evidence-based standard in WHO guidance.

teaching_points.claim: A network meta-analysis found REGN-EB3 and mAb114 each reduced mortality compared with ZMapp, remdesivir or standard care, although certainty was low or very low in most comparisons.
WHO therapeutics guidance emphasises recommended monoclonal antibodies together with optimised supportive care, and gives practical guidance on administration.
The WHO guideline on clinical management of filovirus disease stresses timely assessment, individualised treatment and integration with infection prevention and control.
Case fatality for Ebola disease remains high and heterogeneous, so early diagnosis, early treatment where available and supportive care are important.
Survivors have persistent somatic symptoms; arthralgia, myalgia and abdominal pain decrease over time while headache, fatigue, numbness and hearing loss increase.
ACIP recommends Ervebo vaccine for specified at-risk groups such as responders and laboratory staff at biosafety level 4 facilities.

page.mentor_intro: Acute ECG interpretation is time-critical, particularly in STEMI, where prehospital ECG transmission and short ECG-to-device times improve survival. Retrieval gave STEMI-focused evidence and no general ECG interpretation source, so this page is limited.

teaching_points.claim: Prehospital digital ECG transmission in STEMI networks reduced door-to-device and first-medical-contact-to-device times and was associated with 47% lower mortality (OR 0.53).
ECG-diagnosis-to-sheath time under 90 minutes was associated with lower 30-day mortality (10.5% versus 17.7%), with a number needed to prevent one death of 39 overall and 14 in the elderly.

In inferior STEMI, ST elevation in III greater than II together with ST depression in aVL greater than I may be the most accurate and convenient ECG method to identify the culprit artery; complex algorithms were not superior.
Updated considerations for ECG screening of young athletes address early repolarisation, left atrial abnormality, right bundle branch block, ST shifts and high and low QRS voltage.

uncertainties: Basic systematic ECG interpretation (rate, rhythm, axis, intervals) and life-threatening arrhythmias are not covered by retrieved abstracts.

teaching_points.claim: The EuroGuiDerm living guideline covers conventional immunosuppressants (azathioprine, ciclosporin, glucocorticosteroids, methotrexate, mycophenolate), biologics (dupilumab, lebrikizumab, nemolizumab, tralokinumab) and JAK inhibitors (abrocitinib, baricitinib, upadacitinib), with attention to paediatric, adolescent and pregnant patients.
The 2025 AAD focused update made strong recommendations for tapinarof cream, roflumilast cream, lebrikizumab and nemolizumab with concomitant topical therapy in adults.
Most trials of atopic dermatitis therapy are short, which limits conclusions about long-term comparative efficacy and safety.
The German-language S3 guideline Part 2 covers systemic treatment, including dupilumab, tralokinumab, JAK inhibitors, ciclosporin and systemic glucocorticoids.

uncertainties: Long-term comparative safety of biologics versus JAK inhibitors.

page.mentor_intro: eGFR equations estimate filtration from creatinine and/or cystatin C; accuracy is limited in extremes of body composition and disease. Moving to race-free equations and adding cystatin C or measured GFR improves decisions.

teaching_points.claim: US pharmacy and medication-safety bodies advise moving from Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance to race-free eGFR equations for medication-related decisions, for more accurate and consistent assessment.

In patients with cancer, eGFR should incorporate both creatinine and cystatin C, and measured GFR with an exogenous filtration marker should be considered when eGFR gives borderline eligibility for therapy or trials.

Creatinine-based eGFR equations underestimate renal clearance in patients with sarcopenia or severe muscle wasting and overestimate clearance in muscular individuals; the 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine-cystatin C combined equation significantly improves diagnostic accuracy without using race variables.

Measured GFR using exogenous tracers (iohexol, 51Cr-EDTA, or iothalamate) remains the definitive reference standard in oncology for nephrotoxic chemotherapies (such as cisplatin and high-dose methotrexate) where narrow therapeutic indices preclude estimation errors.

uncertainties: Impact of muscle mass, obesity and acute illness on creatinine-based eGFR is not covered in these sources.
mcq_angles: Why cystatin C adds value in sarcopenia or cancer.

page.mentor_intro: Electrical storm needs urgent antiarrhythmic therapy, sedation and treatment of triggers; for refractory cases, sympathetic modulation (stellate ganglion block, cardiac sympathetic denervation, renal denervation) and catheter ablation are options.

teaching_points.claim: The EHRA 2024 consensus covers pathophysiology, presentation, diagnostic evaluation and acute and long-term management of electrical storm and clustered ventricular arrhythmias.

A systematic review found stellate ganglion blockade significantly decreased ventricular arrhythmia burden (12.4 to 1.04 episodes per day) in electrical storm, though larger prospective studies are needed; a later meta-analysis of observational data agrees.
Cardiac sympathetic denervation was associated with 60% VT non-recurrence at mean 15-month follow-up and fewer ICD shocks.
Renal denervation reduced ICD therapies in refractory ventricular arrhythmias and electrical storm, although randomised data are lacking.
In CPVT, ICD use is associated with high shock burden and complications, and adherence to guideline-directed adjuvant antiarrhythmic therapy is poor.
The 2022 ESC ventricular arrhythmia guideline added new recommendations for Brugada syndrome and primary electrical disease.

uncertainties: Sympathetic modulation evidence is observational.

page.mentor_intro: This topic is very broad. The retrieved sources deal with hyperkalaemia in patients who need RAAS inhibitors, and hyponatraemia work-up in cirrhosis. A narrower scope is needed before a useful page can be approved.

teaching_points.claim: Consensus panels in the US and Japan advise treating RAAS-inhibitor-induced hyperkalaemia in heart failure and CKD while maintaining optimal RAASi therapy, to preserve the cardiovascular benefit of these drugs.

In cirrhosis with hyponatraemia, the AGA expert review advises reviewing diuretic and medication history, electrolytes and kidney function, GI bleeding, and infection including diagnostic paracentesis.

Novel potassium-binding polymers (patiromer and sodium zirconium cyclosilicate, SZC) facilitate sustained maintenance of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) with ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists in patients with heart failure and CKD who develop hyperkalemia.

Hypervolemic hyponatremia in decompensated cirrhosis reflects non-osmotic hypersecretion of arginine vasopressin driven by severe effective arterial underfilling; fluid restriction (1,000-1,500 mL/day) is indicated when serum sodium drops below 125 mmol/L, avoiding rapid correction that risks osmotic demyelination syndrome.

uncertainties: Treatment algorithms for each electrolyte are not covered.
mcq_angles: Managing hyperkalaemia while keeping RAAS inhibitors.
case_hooks: Heart failure patient on spironolactone with potassium 5.9.

page.mentor_intro: Empagliflozin reduces cardiovascular and kidney events across diabetes, heart failure and CKD populations, with a well-characterised safety profile. Kidney benefit does not depend on diabetes status or the early eGFR dip.

teaching_points.claim: An individual-participant meta-analysis of four large trials confirmed the long-term safety and tolerability of empagliflozin.
Empagliflozin's kidney benefits were evident irrespective of the size of the acute eGFR dip, diabetes status, heart failure status and primary cause of kidney disease.
SGLT2 inhibitors help delay progression of non-diabetic chronic kidney disease.

In type 2 diabetes, network meta-analysis suggested empagliflozin might be better than other SGLT2 inhibitors for all-cause mortality and cardiovascular events, and may be preferred in patients without CKD; these are indirect comparisons.
Empagliflozin and dapagliflozin may reduce the relative risk of sudden cardiac death in adjudicated trial data.

uncertainties: Indirect comparisons between SGLT2 inhibitors; ad hoc RCTs needed.

page.mentor_intro: Early appropriate empirical antimicrobials, cultures before antibiotics and prompt source control are the pillars of sepsis care. Most supporting recommendations rest on low-certainty evidence, so they are mostly weak recommendations or best practice statements.

teaching_points.claim: The ESCMID emergency-department antimicrobial stewardship guideline states most recommendations rest on very low or low certainty evidence, leading to weak recommendations or best practice statements.

A scoping review of source control in bloodstream infection in sepsis found inconsistent definitions and poor efficacy assessment, with catheter-source infections and candidaemia over-represented; standardised reporting is needed.

In neonates at risk of early-onset sepsis, antibiotics should be stopped as early as possible within the first 24 hours when sepsis is not confirmed, and therapy should be streamlined when infection is proven.
The Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 paediatric guideline highlights flexibility, early recognition, cautious intervention and long-term recovery, and recognises large evidence gaps.
The Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 adult guidelines remain the international reference for management of sepsis and septic shock.

uncertainties: Optimal timing of antibiotics in uncertain sepsis; benefits of source control are poorly quantified.
mcq_angles: Blood cultures before antibiotics provided it does not delay therapy.
Why antibiotics should be reviewed and streamlined at 24-48 hours.
case_hooks: Febrile hypotensive patient with abdominal pain: empirical regimen and source control.
page.gaps: Specific empirical regimens by source, local-resistance adjustment, and time-to-antibiotic targets are not in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Enalapril established ACE inhibitors as foundational therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: CONSENSUS and SOLVD showed lower mortality and fewer heart failure hospitalisations, and SOLVD Prevention showed benefit even in asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction.

teaching_points.claim: CONSENSUS concluded that adding enalapril to conventional therapy in severe congestive heart failure can reduce mortality and improve symptoms, the effect on mortality coming from fewer deaths from progression of heart failure.
SOLVD Treatment showed enalapril added to conventional therapy significantly reduced mortality and hospitalisations for heart failure in chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
SOLVD Prevention showed enalapril reduced the incidence of heart failure and related hospitalisations in asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction, with a trend toward fewer cardiovascular deaths.
Contemporary HFrEF therapies (ARBs, ARNIs, SGLT2 inhibitors, ivabradine, hydralazine-nitrate and IV iron) improved health-related quality of life.
Guideline-recommended therapies since 2015 reduced mortality and morbidity except digoxin, which reduced only heart failure hospitalisation.
GDMT should not be inappropriately held during heart failure hospitalisation; discharge tools and post-discharge titration clinics help keep regimens optimised.

page.mentor_intro: Antibiotic prophylaxis before invasive dental procedures lowers endocarditis risk in high-risk individuals but not in low-risk people, consistent with AHA and ESC recommendations. Treatment follows the 2023 ESC guideline, which added early surgery for prosthetic valve endocarditis.

teaching_points.claim: A 2024 meta-analysis found antibiotic prophylaxis before invasive dental procedures was associated with lower infective endocarditis incidence in high-risk individuals, with no proven association in low or unknown risk groups, supporting AHA and ESC recommendations.
The 2023 ESC guideline includes a new class I recommendation for surgery in early (under 6 months) prosthetic valve endocarditis and guidance on device reimplantation after cardiac device infection.

Outpatient parenteral antibiotic therapy in selected endocarditis patients had low mortality and relapse rates but more readmissions and IV-line complications, so patient selection and monitoring matter.
An AHA advisory summarises percutaneous mechanical aspiration for right-sided infective endocarditis and provides consensus on patient selection.
A review of MRSA bacteraemia treatment covers available agents, knowledge gaps and recent developments.

uncertainties: Population-level benefit of dental prophylaxis in lower-risk groups.
mcq_angles: Who needs antibiotic prophylaxis before dental work (prosthetic valve, previous IE, certain congenital disease).
Indications for early surgery.
case_hooks: Patient with a mechanical aortic valve needing a dental extraction.
page.gaps: The NICE position (no routine prophylaxis) differs from AHA/ESC and is not in the retrieved abstracts; the explicit list of high-risk cardiac lesions is also not stated.

Mortality in primary adrenal insufficiency is increased about 2.5-fold, and in congenital adrenal hyperplasia the main cause of death is adrenal crisis.
A 2026 joint consensus statement standardises the management of thyroid storm, including treatment of the underlying hyperthyroidism after stabilisation.
In pituitary apoplexy, patients without severe visual or neurological deficits can be managed expectantly, with management individualised to presenting severity.
