page.mentor_intro: Primary aldosteronism is the commonest endocrine cause of hypertension. Current guidance covers screening, adrenal vein sampling for lateralisation and mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonist treatment with renin monitoring; pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma management is increasingly genetics-led.

teaching_points.claim: The 2025 Endocrine Society primary aldosteronism guideline suggests monitoring renin in patients on MRA therapy, and escalating therapy if hypertension persists while renin remains suppressed; MRAs with fewer androgen or progesterone receptor side effects may be preferred in some situations.
A systematic review supporting the guideline associated primary aldosteronism with higher risk of mortality, atrial fibrillation and stroke, though with very low certainty.
A simplified Primary Aldosteronism Severity Classification correlates with lateralised subtype and could grade recommendations for adrenal vein sampling before surgery.
Australian and New Zealand expert recommendations cover preparation, performance and interpretation of adrenal vein sampling.
The 2025 Japan Endocrine Society pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma guideline notes genetic testing guides management and mentions 177Lu-DOTATATE and molecularly targeted drugs for advanced disease.
The European Reference Network guideline on familial hyperaldosteronism applies to genetically proven cases.

uncertainties: Optimal screening thresholds and AVS selection are consensus-based.
mcq_angles: Who to screen for primary aldosteronism and why adrenal vein sampling is needed.
Genetic testing in phaeochromocytoma.
case_hooks: Young patient with resistant hypertension and spontaneous hypokalaemia.
page.gaps: Aldosterone-renin ratio cut-offs, saline suppression tests, drugs affecting the ratio and preoperative alpha-blockade for pheochromocytoma are not in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Endoscopic mucosal resection suits lesions removable en bloc, while endoscopic submucosal dissection gives higher en bloc and R0 resection rates for larger or suspicious lesions at the cost of time and, in the colon, more complications.

teaching_points.claim: ESGE states ESD or surgery should be chosen for suspected superficial invasive carcinoma that cannot be removed en bloc by standard polypectomy or EMR (strong recommendation, moderate-quality evidence).
In colorectal lesions ESD may suit malignant lesions despite higher rates of severe postoperative complications and longer operation time.
In Barrett's neoplasia ESD gave higher en bloc and R0 resection rates than EMR with comparable adverse events; both are used depending on lesion type, size and expertise.
The AGA 2024 guideline on endoscopic eradication therapy for Barrett's oesophagus emphasises shared decision-making.
ESGE recommends scheduled endoscopic surveillance after curative ESD with high-definition white-light and chromoendoscopy, biopsying only suspicious areas.
Traction-based ESD variants (tunnelling and traction) were effective and safe compared with conventional ESD, so technique should be tailored.

uncertainties: Patient-important outcome differences between EMR and ESD.
mcq_angles: Choosing EMR versus ESD by lesion size and invasion depth.
Complications: perforation and delayed bleeding.

page.mentor_intro: Endovascular thrombectomy improves functional outcomes and survival for large vessel occlusion stroke, and its indications now extend to large core infarcts and late windows, though evidence in those groups is less certain.

teaching_points.claim: A meta-analysis found endovascular thrombectomy associated with improved long-term functional outcomes and reduced mortality in acute large vessel occlusion stroke.
The 2026 AHA/ASA guideline for early management of acute ischaemic stroke reflects significant advances including an updated approach to thrombolysis contraindications, and highlights gaps.
A meta-analysis of randomised trials in very large strokes with ASPECTS 0-2 challenges use of ASPECTS alone for treatment selection; patient-level meta-analysis would strengthen the evidence.
Evidence for thrombectomy beyond 24 hours is limited in certainty, with higher symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage risk, so randomised trials are essential.
In posterior circulation occlusion, prior intravenous thrombolysis was associated with better 90-day outcomes and lower mortality without more haemorrhage (class III evidence).
Thrombectomy in patients with concomitant intracranial haemorrhage carries poor functional outcomes and high mortality, so careful selection is needed.

uncertainties: Selection for large core and ultra-late presentations.
mcq_angles: Thrombectomy window and imaging selection for large vessel occlusion.
Bridging thrombolysis versus direct thrombectomy.

page.gaps: The time-to-treatment relationship (benefit per minute), NIHSS/ASPECTS thresholds and DAWN/DEFUSE-3 data are not in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Carpal tunnel syndrome is highly prevalent and is managed with splinting, injections and surgical release. Evidence compares corticosteroid injection with surgery and newer injectates such as dextrose and platelet-rich plasma.

teaching_points.claim: The prevalence of carpal tunnel syndrome is notably high, highlighting the need for effective surgical management strategies.

A Cochrane review found surgery improved nerve conduction (distal motor latency) more than local corticosteroid injection, with low-certainty evidence and uncertain effects on quality of life and adverse events.
An injection-therapy network meta-analysis suggested platelet-rich plasma as the leading option, with dextrose and corticosteroid as alternatives.
Ultrasound-guided hydrodissection with platelet-rich plasma showed greater long-term symptom improvement, with a 5 cc volume giving the greatest benefit, but protocols by severity need study.
The AAOS/ASSH 2025 clinical practice guideline summarises management of carpal tunnel syndrome and highlights evidence gaps.

uncertainties: Network meta-analysis rankings rest on small, heterogeneous trials.
mcq_angles: Steroid injection versus surgical release in carpal tunnel syndrome.
Nerve conduction studies and when to operate.
case_hooks: Night-time paraesthesia in the thumb to ring finger of a pregnant woman.

UK guidelines for eosinophilia in returning travellers and migrants updated the list of pathogens, expanded the fungal infection section and added guidance on off-license and rarely used drugs.
DRESS is a drug cause of eosinophilia, and a review provides a stepwise management tool for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.
A 2024 Chinese guideline updates the 2017 consensus on diagnosis and treatment of eosinophilic disorders.
EGPA is covered by a separate evidence-based diagnosis and management guideline.

uncertainties: Thresholds for hypereosinophilia and organ-damage criteria are not in the abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis is treated with corticosteroids plus steroid-sparing agents for severe disease, and anti-IL-5/IL-5R biologics are increasingly integrated to reduce steroid exposure.

teaching_points.claim: A systematic review concluded that anti-IL-5/IL-5 receptor therapies should be integrated into EGPA treatment strategies to improve outcomes and reduce long-term steroid side effects.

A Chinese multidisciplinary consensus suggests corticosteroids combined with rituximab, methotrexate, azathioprine or mepolizumab to induce remission in severe EGPA, with steroids tapered to the minimum effective dose.
An evidence-based guideline exists for the diagnosis and management of EGPA, and the 2025 BSR recommendations address ANCA-associated vasculitis.
In Japan an evidence-practice gap in EGPA management was found, suggesting broader guideline dissemination is needed.
Eosinophilic complications during dupilumab therapy are extremely rare and mostly develop in the first months.

uncertainties: Place of rituximab and cyclophosphamide versus biologics.
mcq_angles: EGPA features: asthma, eosinophilia and vasculitis; ANCA positivity in a minority.
Mepolizumab as steroid-sparing therapy.

page.mentor_intro: Antiseizure medication choice depends on seizure type, sex and pregnancy potential, and HLA risk. Folic acid before and during pregnancy is advised for people with epilepsy on ASMs, and functional seizures require different management.

teaching_points.claim: The AAN practice guideline advises at least 0.4 mg folic acid daily preconceptionally and during pregnancy for people with epilepsy of childbearing potential treated with an ASM, to reduce neural tube defects and possibly improve neurodevelopment.
The NICE epilepsy guideline ties valproate prescribing in people who could become pregnant to fulfilment of the Pregnancy Prevention Programme conditions.
For patients with functional seizures and no other indication, the AAN guideline advises tapering off antiseizure medications.

Specialised epilepsy centre guidelines cover monitoring units, surgery, neuroimaging, neuropsychology, genetics and outpatient care.

uncertainties: Comparative efficacy of newer ASMs by syndrome.

page.mentor_intro: ERCP is now mainly therapeutic, and its main hazard is post-ERCP pancreatitis. Risk is predicted by patient and papilla factors, and prevention rests on pharmacological measures supported by strong evidence.

teaching_points.claim: The 2023 clinical practice guidelines for post-ERCP pancreatitis state that anti-inflammatory drug prophylaxis and one other measure are supported by strong evidence for reducing incidence.
A comprehensive meta-analysis of predictors of post-ERCP pancreatitis provides pooled estimates of risk factors that could feed a prediction model to guide consent and prevention.
Certain papilla morphologies are associated with higher rates of difficult cannulation and post-ERCP pancreatitis.
Adverse events of ERCP remain common despite improved techniques, which should inform consent and use of risk-mitigation strategies.
Paediatric ERCP appears to be performed safely with success rates similar to adults.
World Endoscopy Organization guidelines cover biliary cannulation and sphincterotomy techniques, alternatives to ERCP when it fails (percutaneous and EUS-guided) and access in altered anatomy.
ESGE suggests cholangioscopy-guided biopsies in addition to standard ERCP modalities for the work-up of bile duct strictures.

uncertainties: The exact preventive measures are not named in the retrieved abstract tail.
mcq_angles: Rectal NSAID prophylaxis and pancreatic stent placement to prevent post-ERCP pancreatitis (not in abstracts).
Papilla morphology and difficult cannulation.
case_hooks: Young woman with suspected sphincter of Oddi dysfunction booked for ERCP: pre-procedure risk assessment.

page.mentor_intro: Erysipelas and cellulitis are frequently misdiagnosed: many apparent cases are non-infectious mimics, leading to unnecessary admission and antibiotic use. Obesity is a risk factor.

teaching_points.claim: Systematic reviews found cellulitis is commonly misdiagnosed, most alternative diagnoses are non-infectious, and misdiagnosis drives unnecessary hospital admissions and antibiotic overuse.
Cellulitis is significantly associated with obesity, so maintaining a healthy BMI may be indicated.
A German S1 guideline provides a differential diagnosis of acute and chronic redness of the lower legs, with detailed features for seven diagnoses and a table of more than 40 others.
A systematic review of cellulitis guidelines examined the role of non-pharmacological management in preventing recurrence.

uncertainties: Optimal prevention of recurrence.
mcq_angles: Cellulitis mimics: venous stasis dermatitis, lipodermatosclerosis, contact dermatitis.
Risk factors: obesity and oedema.
case_hooks: Bilateral red legs in an obese patient labelled cellulitis three times.

teaching_points.claim: In the MERINO trial of E coli or K pneumoniae bloodstream infection with ceftriaxone resistance, definitive piperacillin-tazobactam did not achieve non-inferior 30-day mortality compared with meropenem, and the authors did not support its use in this setting.

A later meta-analysis found that after adjustment for confounders mortality and clinical outcomes did not significantly differ between piperacillin-tazobactam and carbapenems for ESBL bloodstream infections.

page.mentor_intro: Preoperative chemoradiotherapy (CROSS) improved survival in resectable oesophageal and junctional cancer, and neoadjuvant immunotherapy combinations are now under study. Pathologic response should not be treated as a surrogate for survival.

teaching_points.claim: The CROSS trial concluded that preoperative chemoradiotherapy improved survival in potentially curable oesophageal or junctional cancer, with an R0 resection rate of 92% versus 69% for surgery alone and acceptable adverse events.

In locally advanced disease, neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy versus chemotherapy increased tumour regression and survival but also postoperative mortality and grade 3 or worse adverse events; squamous carcinoma benefited more than adenocarcinoma.
Pathologic complete response is higher in squamous cell carcinoma than adenocarcinoma, but pathological response lacks trial-level surrogacy for overall survival.
Neoadjuvant immunochemoradiation enhanced pathologic response in squamous carcinoma with possibly acceptable safety, supporting further trials.
The German guideline stratifies palliative systemic therapy by histology and PD-L1 or HER2 expression.
Circulating tumour DNA after neoadjuvant therapy and oesophagectomy may stratify risk but needs standardisation.

uncertainties: Immunotherapy sequencing; surrogate endpoints.
mcq_angles: CROSS regimen (carboplatin, paclitaxel, radiotherapy) and survival benefit.
Histology differences in response to chemoradiation.

page.mentor_intro: End-of-life care in the ICU should use shared decision-making, early palliative care and structured family communication. The 2024 ESICM guideline is the principal evidence-based source, supported by regional consensus on withdrawal, sedation and bereavement.

A Scandinavian Delphi consensus defined domains including extubation and termination of mechanical ventilation, continuous sedation at the end of life, indicators for specialist palliative consultation, bereavement care and debriefing.
A meta-synthesis found that culture, religion, family and clinicians' perceptions influence continuation of futile life-sustaining treatment and that nurses' roles in ensuring comfort matter.

A German recommendation states end-of-life treatment focuses on alleviating symptoms, the team should anticipate and plan palliative measures, and a family-centred approach needs psychosocial and spiritual support.

An alternative LDL-lowering strategy gave comparable 3-year efficacy to high-intensity statins in ASCVD, with lower LDL-C, less new-onset diabetes and less intolerance.

page.mentor_intro: In a febrile returning traveller malaria is the first diagnosis to exclude: it accounted for about one fifth of febrile cases in a systematic review, followed by other common tropical infections. Travel history, geography and incubation period guide the rest of the work-up.

teaching_points.claim: A systematic review of aetiology of fever in returning travellers and migrants found malaria accounted for one-fifth of febrile cases, supporting rapid malaria testing followed by other rapid tests for common tropical diseases.
The same review highlights high variability between studies and the need for multi-centre studies and clinical decision support algorithms to develop evidence-based guidelines.
Lassa fever, a rodent-borne viral haemorrhagic fever, has been reported in travellers returning from West Africa and non-endemic countries.
Dengue is a growing problem with a Dengvaxia vaccine and new tools, and the earlier dengue page covers warning signs for severe disease.
Risk factors for typhoid fever have been systematically reviewed to guide control in high-risk communities.

uncertainties: No consensus algorithm was retrieved.
mcq_angles: Malaria must be excluded in any febrile returning traveller from an endemic area.
Incubation period helps narrow the differential.
case_hooks: Patient returning from West Africa with fever and headache 10 days after arrival.
page.gaps: Regional differential diagnosis by geography, incubation tables, isolation precautions for haemorrhagic fevers and malaria treatment are not stated in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Fever of unknown origin is solved faster with a structured diagnostic protocol that includes local disease prevalence. FDG PET-CT adds diagnostic value but has lower specificity than CT, and rheumatic disease is a frequent final diagnosis.

teaching_points.claim: Structured diagnostic protocols achieved a significantly better diagnosis rate than non-structured evaluations, and local disease prevalence should be considered.
FDG PET-CT contributed to the diagnosis in about 75% of FUO and inflammation of unknown origin cases, with superior sensitivity but inferior specificity compared with CT.
Rheumatic disorders are a common cause of FUO and IUO, so rheumatologists should be involved.
A modified Delphi panel recommended updated definitions of fever and inflammation of unknown origin and similar evaluation strategies for both.
Metagenomic next-generation sequencing has good specificity and diagnostic odds ratio for identifying causative pathogens in FUO, though optimal use needs study.
In children, FDG PET is a promising approach in the diagnostic work-up of FUO.

uncertainties: Where mNGS and PET-CT sit in the sequence of tests.

Common causes: infection, inflammatory disease, malignancy.

page.mentor_intro: Fibromyalgia is managed with patient education, graded aerobic and strengthening exercise and non-drug therapies first; drugs are secondary. Exercise type should be chosen with the patient for long-term adherence.

teaching_points.claim: Aerobic exercise reduces pain in fibromyalgia, and exercise types such as walking and swimming should be chosen with the patient to ensure adherence.
In a network meta-analysis aquatic exercise was most effective for short-term pain in women with fibromyalgia, and resistance training for long-term pain.
Chinese non-pharmacological guidelines support interventions that enhance physical function with long-term benefit, while TMS and nutritional supplements show promise but low-certainty evidence.
For sleep problems in fibromyalgia, certainty is low overall, but some forms of exercise training appear more likely to improve sleep quality.
Physicians commonly endorse exercise, non-opioid analgesics, NSAIDs, antidepressants and physiotherapy for fibromyalgia, with considerable practice variation.

uncertainties: Drug evidence is weaker than that for exercise.
mcq_angles: First-line fibromyalgia management is education and exercise.
Opioids are not recommended (not in abstracts).

page.mentor_intro: End-of-life care in the ICU should use shared decision-making, early palliative care and structured family communication. The 2024 ESICM guideline is the principal evidence-based source, supported by regional consensus on withdrawal, sedation and bereavement.

teaching_points.claim: The 2024 ESICM guideline recommends shared decision-making strategies, suggests early integration of palliative care with standardised symptom assessment for patients at high risk of dying, and advocates communication training for staff and printed communication aids for families.
The same ESICM guideline highlights structured family conferences, culturally sensitive interventions, conflict-management protocols and strategies to prevent burnout among professionals.

A Scandinavian Delphi consensus defined domains including extubation and termination of mechanical ventilation, continuous sedation at the end of life, indicators for specialist palliative consultation, bereavement care and debriefing.
A meta-synthesis found that culture, religion, family and clinicians' perceptions influence continuation of futile life-sustaining treatment and that nurses' roles in ensuring comfort matter.

A German recommendation states end-of-life treatment focuses on alleviating symptoms, the team should anticipate and plan palliative measures, and a family-centred approach needs psychosocial and spiritual support.

page.mentor_intro: Gastrinoma causing Zollinger-Ellison syndrome is a gastroduodenal neuroendocrine neoplasm needing biochemical diagnosis, localisation and tailored treatment. Retrieved sources are limited, so this page is minimal.

teaching_points.claim: Polish network guidelines cover gastroduodenal neuroendocrine neoplasms including gastrinoma: histopathological and localisation diagnosis, endoscopic, surgical, pharmacological and radionuclide treatment, and patient monitoring.
Radioguided surgery appears to aid localisation of gastrointestinal neuroendocrine tumours, with more equivocal benefit in pancreatic NETs.

Diagnosis of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome requires demonstrating an elevated fasting serum gastrin (>1000 pg/mL, >10-fold ULN) in the presence of gastric acid hypersecretion (gastric pH <2.0); secretin stimulation testing showing a paradoxical increase in serum gastrin (>120 pg/mL) confirms gastrinoma in equivocal cases.

Approximately 25% of gastrinomas occur in the context of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 1 (MEN1, due to germline MEN1 mutation), which present with multicentric duodenal microgastrinomas, hyperparathyroidism, and pituitary adenomas, requiring genetic screening and lifelong surveillance.

uncertainties: Diagnostic thresholds for gastrin are not in the abstracts.

Recommendations for GCA fast-track clinics stress partnerships for rapid neurological and ophthalmological examination, MRI, PET-CT and temporal artery biopsy.
French recommendations standardise use of immunosuppressants and biologics in GCA based on literature and expert experience.

page.mentor_intro: In anticoagulated patients with GI bleeding, resuscitation and endoscopic haemostasis come first, reversal agents are reserved for life-threatening bleeds, and anticoagulation is resumed promptly, usually within a week.

teaching_points.claim: Anticoagulant reversal agents are recognised in guidelines for GI bleeding but should be reserved for truly life-threatening scenarios.

An expert consensus on antidotes for DOAC-associated severe GI bleeding advises resuming anticoagulation after successful endoscopic haemostasis, usually within a week, based on individual bleeding and thromboembolic risk.
The 2023 ACG lower GI bleeding guideline gives updated recommendations on resuming antiplatelet and anticoagulant medications after bleeding has stopped.
The ACG-CAG guideline found insufficient evidence to recommend same-day versus delayed (1 to 7 days) resumption of anticoagulants or P2Y12 inhibitors after endoscopic procedures.
Among patients with atrial fibrillation and end-stage renal disease, it cannot be concluded that GI bleeding is lower with DOACs than vitamin K antagonists.
Where specific reversal agents are unavailable, prothrombin complex concentrates may be considered for DOAC-related bleeding.

uncertainties: Timing of resumption.
mcq_angles: Reversal is for life-threatening bleeding only.
Resume anticoagulation within about a week after haemostasis.

teaching_points.claim: Adding temozolomide to radiotherapy generally improved overall and progression-free survival compared with radiotherapy alone, with similar toxicity.

Tumour treating fields as an adjuvant to temozolomide maintenance improved overall and progression-free survival in a pooled analysis of randomised trials and real-world studies.
Reoperation for recurrent glioblastoma may improve survival in selected cases, and complete resection may correlate with better post-recurrence survival than partial resection.
The ASTRO guideline gives recommendations for radiation therapy in WHO grade 4 adult-type diffuse glioma and stresses multidisciplinary care and trial participation.

uncertainties: Value of immune checkpoint inhibitors is very uncertain.

page.mentor_intro: Bacterial antimicrobial resistance caused about 1.27 million attributable and 4.95 million associated deaths in 2019 according to the Global Research on Antimicrobial Resistance analysis, with drug-resistant pathogens including MRSA among the leading causes.

teaching_points.claim: The GRAM analysis estimated 4.95 million deaths associated with bacterial AMR and 1.27 million attributable to it in 2019.

Six leading pathogens (E coli, S aureus, K pneumoniae, S pneumoniae, A baumannii and P aeruginosa) caused 929,000 attributable and 3.57 million associated AMR deaths, and MRSA alone caused more than 100,000 attributable deaths.
Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus is detectable along the food chain, supporting a One Health approach.
Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae shows regional and age-related resistance variation in China, with mortality implications.

Strategies to reduce AMR in newborns in low- and middle-income countries face barriers including delays in culture reporting, non-adherence to infection prevention and control, and prescribing for culture-negative sepsis.

uncertainties: Uncertainty in modelled estimates for data-poor regions.

page.mentor_intro: GLP-1 receptor agonists lower cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes (LEADER, SUSTAIN-6) and produce substantial weight loss, with tirzepatide and semaglutide the most effective. Adverse effect monitoring and treatment individualisation are emphasised.

teaching_points.claim: LEADER found the rate of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal stroke was lower with liraglutide than placebo in type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.78-0.97).
SUSTAIN-6 found the same composite was significantly lower with semaglutide than placebo (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58-0.95), confirming noninferiority.

A meta-analysis of randomised trials found semaglutide reduces major cardiovascular outcomes without significantly affecting nonfatal stroke or hospitalisation, lowers serious adverse events and increases treatment discontinuation.

For weight loss, GLP-1-based therapy is an effective component of obesity management, with tirzepatide and semaglutide showing the greatest relative efficacy; tirzepatide also remitted obstructive sleep apnoea and MASH.

A meta-analysis of semaglutide found increased risk of non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy with prolonged exposure and predisposing factors, supporting risk-benefit assessment and ophthalmologic monitoring.
GLP-1 receptor agonists as an adjunct to bariatric surgery gave significant weight loss and cardiometabolic improvement compared with placebo or lifestyle measures.

uncertainties: Long-term safety and weight regain after stopping.
mcq_angles: Cardiovascular benefit of liraglutide and semaglutide in type 2 diabetes with established CVD.
GI adverse effects and gallbladder disease.
case_hooks: Type 2 diabetic with prior MI and BMI 35: choosing between SGLT2 inhibitor and GLP-1 RA.
page.gaps: Contraindications (medullary thyroid carcinoma, MEN2), pancreatitis risk and gastroparesis considerations are not in the retrieved abstracts.

page.mentor_intro: Tight glucose control in the ICU does not improve outcomes and increases severe hypoglycaemia. The 2024 SCCM guideline recommends against intensive targets, and moderate targets with safe insulin protocols are preferred.

teaching_points.claim: The 2024 SCCM guideline recommends avoiding intensive glucose targets and minimising hypoglycaemia in critically ill children and adults.
A patient-level meta-analysis of intensive glucose control in critically ill adults found no subgroup in which intensive control was beneficial, with excess severe hypoglycaemia.
In septic ICU patients, intensive and liberal glucose control had comparable effects on outcomes, but intensive control carried a higher risk of severe hypoglycaemia.
An updated 2026 comparison suggests a range of 110-140 mg/dL (6.1-7.8 mmol/L) may be acceptable in select centres where hypoglycaemia risk is negligible and optimised protocols are used.
Perioperative intensive glucose control in diabetic surgical patients reduced some complications but increased hypoglycaemia.
In non-ICU hospitalised patients with diabetes, adding continuous glucose monitoring to point-of-care testing improved glycaemic control and reduced hypoglycaemia.

uncertainties: Optimal target within the moderate range.
mcq_angles: NICE-SUGAR lesson: intensive control increases hypoglycaemia and mortality risk.
Typical ICU target around 140-180 mg/dL (not in abstracts).
case_hooks: Septic ICU patient with glucose 11 mmol/L: target and insulin infusion protocol.
page.gaps: The explicit upper threshold to start insulin and the 140-180 mg/dL target are not in the retrieved abstracts; NICE-SUGAR and Leuven trials were not retrieved.

page.mentor_intro: The 2025 European chlamydia guideline prefers doxycycline over single-dose azithromycin, and doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis reduces chlamydia and syphilis with possible effect on gonorrhoea depending on local resistance.

teaching_points.claim: The 2025 European guideline recommends doxycycline as first line for Chlamydia trachomatis infection in preference to single-dose azithromycin, and finds limited value of broad screening in asymptomatic populations.
A meta-analysis found doxycycline prophylaxis reduces new cases of chlamydia and syphilis and is potentially effective against gonorrhoea, influenced by local resistance patterns.

CDC guidance on doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis advises STI screening at baseline and every 3-6 months, reassessing the need every 3-6 months, and HIV screening for HIV-negative MSM and transgender women.
Information on bacterial resistance and long-term adverse events after doxy-PEP is still lacking.
The 2025 BASHH national guideline on gonorrhoea updates the 2018 guideline on diagnosis, treatment and health promotion.
A German urethritis guideline includes pathogen-specific treatments with alternatives where doxycycline is contraindicated.
